s1.syndrome_frame: Sepsis-like syndrome with flank discomfort and history of urinary tract infections
salient_findings: Fever, chills, and left flank discomfort
Positive blood cultures for Gram-positive rods
key_facts: 42-year-old man
Recurrent urinary tract infections due to neurogenic bladder
Previous right nephrectomy for nonfunctioning pelvic kidney
Chronic hypomagnesemia requiring parenteral magnesium sulfate
Receives treatment at home and local infusion center
Afebrile on initial examination
Serum lactate: 1.0 mmol/L
Serum magnesium: 0.66 mmol/L
Leukocytosis: 11,240 cells × 10⁶/L
Normal urinalysis
Normal chest radiograph
Initial blood cultures positive for Gram-positive rods
Follow-up peripheral blood cultures negative after five days
Mediport cultures positive for Gram-positive rods after three days

shortlist.label: Urinary tract infection with sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurrent urinary tract infections and current presentation with leukocytosis and positive blood cultures

shortlist.label: Pyelonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Flank discomfort and history of urinary tract infections, consistent with upper urinary tract infection

shortlist.label: Central line-associated bloodstream infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive mediport cultures and history of receiving treatment through a mediport, suggesting a possible source of infection

shortlist.label: Mediport infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive cultures from the mediport, indicating a possible infection at the site of the device

shortlist.label: Bacteremia due to Corynebacterium species
shortlist.why_kept: Gram-positive rods in blood cultures, which could be consistent with Corynebacterium species, a known cause of bacteremia

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of receiving treatment through a mediport and the cultures from the mediport were positive for Gram-positive rods, which is consistent with a central line-associated bloodstream infection. The initial blood cultures were also positive, and the follow-up peripheral blood cultures became negative after five days, suggesting that the infection was related to the central line.

rejected.label: Urinary tract infection with sepsis
rejected.why: The urinalysis was normal, which does not support a urinary tract infection.

rejected.label: Pyelonephritis
rejected.why: The patient has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections, but the normal urinalysis and lack of other symptoms do not support pyelonephritis.

rejected.label: Mediport infection
rejected.why: While the mediport cultures were positive, this is more consistent with a central line-associated bloodstream infection rather than a localized mediport infection.

rejected.label: Bacteremia due to Corynebacterium species
rejected.why: The Gram-positive rods were identified, but the specific species was not confirmed as Corynebacterium, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with a central line-associated bloodstream infection.
